raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With rejection sampling on B200, a request can get an out-of-vocabulary or zero-weight final token.

This affects EAGLE, EAGLE3, and NEXTN servers with `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` or block verification (both off by default) at temperature above 0. Sampled DSpark on CUDA and EAGLE on ROCm can reach this kernel with no flag. I did not test ROCm, MUSA, DSpark, DFlash, or UNO.

It is rare: with ordinary `torch.rand` coins on synthetic inputs, `main` returned 94 bad tokens in 138 million draws at vocabulary 32,000, and 4 in 138 million after a top-50 filter. Each request makes one draw per verify step.

The real-output rate is unknown. A Qwen3.5-9B server returned no bad token in 56,052 draws on `main`, too few to show it. Coins forced near 1 in those runs gave 6 zero-weight tokens on `main` and none with this change. With ordinary coins, out-of-vocabulary tokens came only from vocabularies of 32 or less. I found no issue that reports this bug.

On B200, `tl.cumsum` over a tile is not monotonic, so a zero-weight or out-of-vocabulary lane can cross the cutoff. This fix comes from closed #44116 and slows large batches.

No other open PR changes this scan, but #47807 copies it into a small-batch split path that this change does not cover.

All table counts are for `main`.

| Vocabulary | Softmax of Gaussian logits, token-wise and block pooled with the same coins | Same, filtered to top 50 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 17 | 13 in 537 million | 15 in 537 million |
| 129 | 1 in 134 million | 6 in 134 million |
| 4,097 | 5 in 143 million | 9 in 143 million |
| 20,000 | 66 in 67 million | 3 in 67 million |
| 32,000 | 94 in 138 million | 4 in 138 million |
| 154,880 | 47 in 35 million | 0 in 35 million |

## Modifications

Only positive-weight lanes can match the cutoff. If none matches, the scan uses the last positive-weight token, or `VOCAB_SIZE - 1` for an empty residual. An accepted row with a positive token, a NaN, then zeros now returns that token.

## Accuracy Tests

Results cover the kernel in b91e0c89ba against `main` 582168dd7c on B200.

In a separate paired run of 2.86 billion ordinary-coin draws, only final tokens differed (258, each a bad token from `main`, none from this change). New regression tests fail only on `main`.

GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 (TP4, EAGLE 5/1/6, rejection sampling on) scored 97.5% on `main` and 98.0% with this change, one run each, as a no-regression check.

```bash
# sgl-eval 0.1.3
sgl-eval run gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-threads 64 --max-tokens 32768 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --thinking
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Batch 48 is the EAGLE default, and larger batches need a higher `--max-running-requests`.

```text
Eager kernel time, this change against main (not a CUDA graph or TP8)
Vocabularies 32,000 and 154,880             at most about 1% slower
Batch 48, token-wise                        8.9% faster to 0.6% slower

Rejection at 4,097, 8,193, 16,383, 16,385, 50,257, and 65,537
Batch 1,024                                 7.4% to 27.2% slower
Batch 4,096                                 18.2% to 40.0% slower

2-slot block verification (off by default)
50,257 and 65,537, batches 1 to 64          4.0% to 5.9% slower
7,000 (worst timed), batch 2,048            39.3% slower
7,000 (worst timed), batch 4,096, two runs  48.1% and 48.5% slower (A/A -0.2% and 0.0%)

bench_serving on GLM, main and this change, one run each
Concurrency 1, warm sweep                   539 and 537 tok/s
Concurrency 16                              1213 and 1208 tok/s
```

```bash
# Concurrency 1 used --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1.
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 80 --max-concurrency 16 --request-rate inf --temperature 1.0 --seed 42 --flush-cache
```

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

files.patch:
@@ -197,9 +197,12 @@ def speculative_sampling_classic_kernel(
 
             norm_sum += tl.sum(val)
 
-    # Pass 2: CDF. Degenerate residual (norm_sum == 0, i.e. p == q everywhere on
-    # rejection) leaves the cumsum at 0 <= target_u, so final_token falls back to
-    # VOCAB_SIZE - 1; acceptable since this case is numerically near-impossible.
+    # Pass 2: CDF. FP32 rounding can move the cumsum across target_u at a zero-weight
+    # lane or at a lane past VOCAB_SIZE, so only positive-weight lanes can match. If
+    # target_u reaches the cumsum total, no lane matches and the last positive-weight
+    # token is used. Degenerate residual (norm_sum == 0, i.e. p == q everywhere on
+    # rejection) has no such token, so final_token falls back to VOCAB_SIZE - 1.
+    # This case is numerically near-impossible.
     target_u = coin_final * norm_sum
     cum_sum = 0.0
     final_token = VOCAB_SIZE - 1
@@ -226,13 +229,22 @@ def speculative_sampling_classic_kernel(
             block_cumsum = tl.cumsum(val, axis=0)
             total_cumsum = cum_sum + block_cumsum
 
-            candidates_mask = total_cumsum > target_u
-            has_match = tl.max(candidates_mask, axis=0)
+            # One reduction finds both results. A match ranks above every other lane
+            # and an earlier match ranks higher. Other positive lanes rank by token.
+            positive = val > 0.0
+            ranks = tl.where(positive, v_offsets, -1)
+            ranks = tl.where(
+                positive & (total_cumsum > target_u),
+                2 * VOCAB_SIZE - 1 - v_offsets,
+                ranks,
+            )
+            best_rank = tl.max(ranks, axis=0)
 
-            if has_match:
-                match_idx = tl.argmax(candidates_mask.to(tl.int32), axis=0)
-                final_token = v_start + match_idx
+            if best_rank >= VOCAB_SIZE:
+                final_token = 2 * VOCAB_SIZE - 1 - best_rank
                 found = 1
+            elif best_rank >= 0:
+                final_token = best_rank
 
             cum_sum += tl.sum(val)

@@ -139,6 +139,59 @@ def test_matches_reference(steps, vocab, block):
     assert (final_coins <= upper + 1e-6).all()
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("vocab,token", [(129, 126), (65569, 32766)])
+def test_final_draw_when_cutoff_rounds_to_residual_total(vocab, token):
+    """The final token must be the last positive-weight token when FP32 rounding
+    lifts the cutoff to the residual total. The scan used to match no token here
+    and return VOCAB_SIZE - 1, which has zero weight."""
+    target = torch.zeros(1, 2, vocab, device=DEVICE)
+    # The common prefix sums to 1 - 2**-126; the two rows differ only in the tail.
+    target[:, :, :126] = target.new_tensor([2.0**-k for k in range(1, 127)])
+    target[:, :, token] = 2.0**-126
+    draft = target[:, :1].clone()
+    draft[:, :, token + 1] = draft[:, :, token]
+    draft[:, :, token] = 0
+    lengths, output = _verify(
+        target,
+        draft,
+        torch.full((1, 2), token + 1, device=DEVICE),
+        target.new_full((1, 2), 0.9),
+        target.new_tensor([1 - 2**-24]),
+        block=False,
+    )
+    assert lengths.item() == 0
+    assert output[0, 0].item() == token
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("vocab", [17, 129])
+def test_final_draw_stays_in_residual_support_for_coins_near_one(vocab):
+    """The final token must have positive residual weight for coins just below 1.
+    FP32 rounding used to let the scan return a zero-weight or out-of-vocabulary
+    token for these coins."""
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    batch = 102400
+    target = torch.randn(batch, 2, vocab, device=DEVICE).softmax(-1)
+    draft = torch.randn(batch, 1, vocab, device=DEVICE).softmax(-1)
+    # Reject the only draft, so the final token comes from max(p - q, 0).
+    candidates = torch.zeros(batch, 2, dtype=torch.long, device=DEVICE)
+    candidates[:, 1] = (draft[:, 0] - target[:, 0]).argmax(-1)
+    # FP32 rounding can lift the cutoff to the cumsum for these largest coins.
+    final_coins = 1 - (torch.arange(batch, device=DEVICE) % 16 + 1) * 2.0**-24
+    lengths, output = _verify(
+        target,
+        draft,
+        candidates,
+        target.new_full((batch, 2), 1 - 2**-24),
+        final_coins,
+        block=False,
+    )
+    assert (lengths == 0).all()
+    tokens = output[:, 0].long()
+    assert ((tokens >= 0) & (tokens < vocab)).all()
+    rows = torch.arange(batch, device=DEVICE)
+    assert (target[rows, 0, tokens] > draft[rows, 0, tokens]).all()
+
+
 def test_accepts_longer_prefix_after_rejection():
     target = torch.tensor([[[1 / 3, 2 / 3]] * 3], device=DEVICE)
     draft = torch.tensor([[[2 / 3, 1 / 3]] * 2], device=DEVICE)
